slides.title: What Happened Saturday
slides.body: On Nov 21, President Trump said on Fox News he would work with the incoming Democratic Congress to cap credit card interest at 10%. He first proposed a one-year cap in January, but no cap was ever enacted.

slides.title: Card Rate vs Proposed Cap
slides.subtitle: Interest rate, percent per year
slides.body: Fed average on accounts paying interest, Q3 2026 (preliminary). Card balances: about $1.285 trillion.

slides.title: Why It Matters
slides.body: Banks oppose a cap, warning of lower limits and closed accounts. A bill still needs Congress, and Democrats take control of both chambers in January. Researchers cited by AP estimate savings near $100 billion a year.

slides.title: Save This: What to Watch Next
items: Dec 8-9: Fed meeting, a rate hike is widely expected
January: new Congress; watch for a card cap bill
